thread.title: Apple Faces 'Gloom And Doom' Ahead Of March-Quarter Report

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Faces 'Gloom And Doom' Ahead Of March-Quarter Report
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) faces a big test with its March-quarter report, due out after the market close Tuesday: Can it calm investors with its outlook for the current quarter and year ahead?
X "Gloom and doom" talk about Apple has reached "deafening levels," Monness Crespi Hardt analyst Brian White said in a note to clients Wednesday. He urged investors to stay the course, reiterating his buy rating on the stock with a price target of 235.
Apple stock climbed 0.5% to close at 163.65 on the stock market today . Shares had fallen in five straight trading sessions through Tuesday.
GBH Insights analyst Daniel Ives said Tuesday that Wall Street had gone into " full panic mode " over Apple.

"After record performance from major Apple suppliers in the second half of 2017, the negativity from the Apple supply chain has reached deafening levels over the past week," White said. "Moreover, errant calls for a 'super cycle' with the iPhone X set unrealistic expectations. As such, Apple's stock has fallen by 11% from its peak in March."
Apple stock has been pressured by concerns of slowing iPhone sales as the smartphone market matures.
Several chipmakers, most notably Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ), have cited smartphone sales weakness in their guidance for at least the first half of 2018.
White cautioned that the March quarter is the seasonally weakest period for Apple.
Apple Earnings Estimates Wall Street is predicting Apple will earn $2.69 a share, up 28% year over year, on sales of $60.98 billion, up 15%, in its fiscal second quarter.
The Cupertino, Calif.-based company also is expected to update its capital return plan on Tuesday. Analysts are expecting a big boost in share buybacks and dividends.
For the June quarter, analysts currently expect Apple to earn $2.16 a share, up 29%, on sales of $52.04 billion, up 15%.
Guggenheim analyst Robert Cihra on Tuesday lowered his iPhone sales expectations for this year and next. He now expects flat unit sales in fiscal 2018 and 2019, vs. his prior outlook for growth of 3% and 5%, respectively.
"Apple ultimately cannot outgrow what is now a no-growth smartphone market," Cihra said in a note to clients.
Apple's iPhone revenue will get a boost from higher average selling prices for its handsets, Cihra said. He predicted Apple's smartphone revenue will rise 14% year over year in fiscal 2018, which ends Sept. 29.
With the smartphone market peaking, Apple will need to target other markets for growth, he said. In the near term, that will be services and other products such as Apple Watch, Air Pods and HomePod. In the long term, that could be media and autos, he said.
Cihra reiterated his buy rating on the stock with a price target of 215.
Meanwhile, Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook was scheduled to meet privately with President Donald Trump on Wednesday afternoon. The agenda for the meeting was not released. Potential topics could include the China-U.S. trade dispute, CNBC said .
